problems: Decided on its own that `--top 0` is a usage error, gave no reason, and asked no question; Saad had to correct it.
The report opens with line-ending (CRLF/LF) back-and-forth, including 'my earlier check was wrong'. This is noise for the user.
When fixing `--top 0` it did not say the new behaviour reversed its own earlier decision, though it did say which test it replaced and why.
The shared `run_main` helper now also asserts exit status 0. This is reasonable, but it quietly widens what every existing caller tests (it is mentioned only in passing).
Asked no questions. It picked `--top 0` = empty and exit 0, and negative = error, and stated these as edge cases without giving reasons. The guesses were right by luck.
The rejection test covers only `-1`: there is no non-numeric case, no check that stderr names `--top`, and no check that stdout is empty.
`test_top_zero_prints_nothing` does not check the exit code (`_run` discards the return value).
The README line does not say N must be 0 or more, or what `--top 0` does.
Heavy ceremony for a roughly 10-line change: a plan doc, a progress doc, two approval rounds, reviewer subagents and a work branch for one CLI flag.
The plan proposed treating `--top 0` as an error, so a correction round was needed (it was at least explained with a reason and caught before any code).
The final state is confusing: the code sits on `[workflow]/top-n/work`, while `feat/top-n` (the branch the user approved) has no code, and a workflow topic is left open that will block future work.
The plan doc still says `Status: draft` despite being approved, and the `default=None` that the reviewer flagged as redundant was left in the code.
The closing messages are full of workflow jargon (`/[workflow]:finish`, `topic end`, squash notes) that Saad did not ask for.

summary: X and Y both wrote the same minimal slice-after-sort code. X ended with complete, focused tests and a precise README after one correction, while Y guessed the edge cases right but tested invalid input only partly. Z handled the change request cleanly, with retired spec lines and updated docs, but buried a trivial feature under plans, reviews and branch machinery, and left the code off the branch the user approved.
